title: Who Pays for the 500 Million COVID Doses? Section 1498 in Arbutus v. Moderna - Patently-O
content:
Arbutus Biopharma Corp. v. Moderna, Inc., No. 26-1581, oral args set for Nov 5 at the Federal Circuit. You may recognize Moderna as key COVID vaccine developer/distributor.  Arbutus holds patents on lipid nanoparticle technology that Moderna used for its vaccine (without a license). The US govt bought about 500 million doses from Moderna that were distributed to the public. The question on appeal is whether Moderna owes the money for infringement; or does the US govt under 28 U.S.C. § 1498(a). Were the COVID-19 vaccine doses that the federal government bought from Moderna and gave to the public made "for the Government"? If so, the Fed Govt takes responsibility for paying under Section 1498(a), and the case would need to be pursued in the Court of Federal Claims (CFC), with the United States as the defendant. If not, Moderna pays - something like $1.3 billion. To continue reading, become a Patently-O member. Already a member? Simply log in to access the full post. title: Tioga v. Teraflex ‘Roller Coaster Road’ trial continued to 2027 - Williston Herald
content:
TIOGA — Court documents obtained by the Williston Herald confirm that the Northwest Judicial District Court has continued the scheduled dates for the long-awaited Tioga v. Teraflex trial by two months, delaying the trial’s start date from Dec. 14 to Feb. 8, 2027. This is the second time the trial has seen a continuance. Following the lawsuit’s filing on April 25, 2024, a July 29, 2024 notice originally scheduled the trial to start on March 9. This date was then pushed back to Dec. 14 in a notice dated Nov. 13, 2025. As of the most recent notice filed on Tuesday, however, the trial’s updated start date is scheduled for Feb. 8, 2027, with five days set aside for the trial extending to Feb. 12, 2027. As covered more extensively in 
    
      prior reporting
    
      , Tioga alleges through the lawsuit that Teraflex breached its contract in which it agreed to complete a reconstruction project on South Main Street. The majority of work was completed in 2021, with remaining punch list items being completed in 2022. After completion of work, however, Tioga officials alleged “severe settlement and/or heaving” throughout the street, with the road earning the nickname “Roller Coaster Road” for its bumpy surface. On Tuesday, this reporter tested out the road in question, confirming that driving at the posted speed limit of 25 miles per hour led to a bouncy ride during certain segments that could be associated with a roller coaster ride. In a third-party complaint originally filed on March 4, 2025 and amended on Sept. 12, 2025, Teraflex alleged that the project’s defects were the fault of subcontractors Terracon Consultants and Keller Paving & Landscaping. As such, Teraflex requested indemnification so that the subcontractors would be responsible for any ordered monetary compensation. On Oct. 22, all involved parties convened for a partial summary judgment hearing before Judge Chas Neff, Jr. On Oct. 27, Teraflex filed a notice requesting an expedited motion to grant a trial continuance. In the motion, Teraflex argued that the continuance was necessary for it to adequately prepare for the trial in reaction to Neff’s partial summary judgment, which had not yet been declared. As the trial’s motion in limine deadline for all parties to include or exclude evidence was this Wednesday, Teraflex requested an expedited response by the preceding Monday. The court split the difference between these two dates, missing the requested response date by a day but still making the cut before the motion in limine deadline through a granted expedited motion on Tuesday. Through the motion, Neff preliminarily reset the trial’s start date and time to 9 a.m. on Feb. 8, 2027 to allow all parties adequate time to react to his still-awaited partial summary judgment. The pre-trial conference was likewise delayed from Dec. 4 to Jan. 29, 2027, also at 9 a.m. Also in the expedited motion, Neff ordered all parties to work together to adjust pre-trial deadlines (but not dispositive motion deadlines) to ensure these updated deadlines don’t conflict with the updated trial date. If the trial sticks to this third start date, it will take place nearly three years after the lawsuit’s original filing and nearly one year after its original start date. Special meeting heldThe Tioga City Commission held a two-minute special meeting on Oct. 30 to address two items that couldn’t wait until its next regular meeting on Nov. 9. Commissioner Cody Normark was absent from the meeting. All other commissioners called in remotely, resulting in the meeting’s recording consisting of an empty room filled by disembodied voices, perhaps appropriate for the following day’s Halloween celebrations. The first item of business was to hire Elijah Clark as a part-time assistant for the Tioga Community Center, which the commission approved with Clark’s effective start date as this upcoming Monday. Commission President Brett Rieniets said that Center Director Joy Sparks interviewed all candidates and landed on Clark as her pick for the job. The commission also approved the city’s transition to winter landfill hours, which are mostly reduced to appointment-only times to meet the colder months’ reduced traffic. As posted on Tioga’s 
    
      Facebook page
    
      , those wanting to schedule a time to dump items can call Street Supervisor Jason Steele at (701) 641-1413 to do so. Drop-offs can be scheduled between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The landfill will also be open with no need for prior appointments from 9 a.m. to noon on the first Saturday of each winter month. title: Nearly 100 Honda CR-V Owners Told NHTSA Their Washers Can’t Clear the Windshield, But Dealers Call It Normal “Wet Arm” Design - Torque News
content: Nearly 100 owners of 2023 to 2025 Honda CR-Vs have filed NHTSA complaints about wipers and washers that cannot keep the windshield clear, and winter is about to make it worse. The issue centers on Honda's "wet arm" design, which sprays washer fluid from the wiper arms, and some owners say dealers have dismissed it as normal operation. Autoblog recently flagged the same Honda CR-V windshield washer problem. Here is what owners report, what we have asked Honda, and what you can do before the snow arrives. Given how important a clean windshield is to safety, this one caught my eye. The issue appears to come from the washer design itself, which a recall or service bulletin may not easily fix. It is hard to believe something like this slipped through, given how much testing goes into every redesign. Yet owners of the redesigned CR-V say it did. How the Honda CR-V's Wet Arm Washers Work, and What Owners Report On the current CR-V, the washer nozzles sit on the wiper arms instead of under the hood. Owners and Autoblog say the spray starts only partway through the wiper's sweep, which makes it harder to clear the whole windshield, especially in snow and ice. Many owners would rather have hood-mounted nozzles that spray the glass before the wipers move. Owners of older CR-V models will remember that setup. One owner described the problem on Reddit. As always, internet comments are edited for content, clarity, and grammar. "I drove in some nasty weather yesterday, and there's one spot on the passenger side that the blade never touches. Even the driver's side doesn't work that well." "I tried the washer to clean it, and it still doesn't reach that spot, even while parked with no ice or snow built up. A shop told me they couldn't replace the wiper without another part, so I have a dealer appointment." "This is a terrible design, and my 1989 Nissan Hardbody had better wipers and sprayers. Give me hood-mounted sprayers, Honda." They weren't the only one. "I will die on this hill, because the wipers, especially when I use washer fluid, are my only gripe about this car," another owner said. "I would pay good money for hood-mounted sprayers," that owner added. Owners also report that the driver's side wiper does not reach the edge of the windshield while driving. Some say it reaches farther in accessory mode, but that does not help on the road, since the car is in run mode when you drive. Nearly 100 NHTSA Complaints and Dealers Who Call It Normal Complaint trackers that pull NHTSA data list 44 visibility and wiper complaints for the 2023 CR-V, 32 for the 2024, and 20 for the 2025. Not every complaint involves the washer design, but many describe the same wet arm behavior. One 2024 owner told NHTSA the dealer dismissed the problem as "normal wet arm operation." A 2025 owner said the dealer checked other CR-Vs on the lot and found they all behaved the same way. Winter makes it harder. One owner wrote that on a cross-country trip in below-zero temperatures, the washer lines on the wiper arms froze, leaving the windshield smeared in heavy traffic. Honda is also studying a related washer issue. It asked dealers to collect washer motors from certain 2023 to 2024 CR-Vs with inoperative or leaking washer systems, to understand the cause before repairs. Torque News has asked Honda whether the wet arm design is working as intended and whether any changes are planned. We will update this story with Honda's response. Because visibility is a safety issue, NHTSA could open an investigation if complaints keep coming. For now there is no recall, and some owners believe Honda will not change the design until the all-new 2028 CR-V. That model may even go hybrid only. Many owners hope the redesign brings back hood-mounted sprayers too. How Honda CR-V Owners Can Cope With the Washer Problem This Winter Use a winter-rated washer fluid so the lines on the wiper arms are less likely to freeze. Clear snow and ice from the wiper arms before you drive. Clean the windshield by hand before long trips, especially in salty or slushy conditions. A clean start means the washers have less work to do. If you are shopping a current CR-V, new or used, spray the washers during the test drive and watch how far the wipers reach. You may not get the chance to test it in bad weather, so ask current owners as well. The washer issue applies to every current CR-V, so it belongs in your decision whether you buy a gas or hybrid CR-V. It sits alongside other ownership questions, like Honda's head gasket warranty extension. Some owners already plan their ownership around those issues. Take the CR-V Hybrid owner who plans to sell at 10 years over the head gasket. Others are watching what comes next, and CR-V Hybrid owners have 3 questions Honda needs to answer about the new model. Honda is clearly committed to the nameplate, with plans to make the CR-V Hybrid its most popular model. title: Perry Sweeps Byron-Bergen to Win Section V Class C2 Girls Volleyball Championship - The Batavian
content: Perry defeated Byron-Bergen in straight sets Tuesday to capture the Section V Class C2 girls volleyball championship. The Yellowjackets won by scores of 25-15, 25-18 and 25-19 to improve to 17-2. Byron-Bergen finished its season with a 13-3 record. Perry used strong play at the net to control the match. Byron-Bergen challenged the Yellowjackets in the second set, briefly taking a 15-14 lead before Perry rallied to win the set, 25-18. In the third set, Perry built a 15-5 advantage behind a service run from Astrid Bellamy. The Yellowjackets maintained the lead to close out the match, 25-19. Zanyah Yisreal led Perry's attack at the net, while Bellamy's serving helped the Yellowjackets pull away in the third set. Perry advances to the Class C crossover game against Class C1 champion Le Roy at 6 p.m. Friday at Avon High School. title: What If a ’53 Cadillac and Corvette Became One 9.2L V-12 Hot Rod? - HOT ROD Network
content:
With 12 cylinders under the body and a 1953 Cadillac vibe, this baby-blue ’Vette rocks. It was the 2021 SEMA Show when Dave Kindig and Kindig-it Design first launched his line of CF1 Corvettes on the MotorTrend SEMA stage. The idea was a modern, built-from-scratch, carbon-bodied hot rod based on the iconic 1953 Corvette. Since those initial roadsters, Kindig has gone on to craft many different versions including cabriolets and fastbacks. We imagine he’s always thinking about fresh takes on his very cool initial concept. The original CF1 featured a Lingenfelter LS7, but this time around, Kindig wanted to go bigger for his next carbon-fiber-bodied “1953” CF1 Corvette. Yep, that means CF1 Fastback #30 being unveiled at the 2026 SEMA Show will have a V-12 under the bonnet. But the bigger visual change is that Kindig wanted to mix in a 1953 Cadillac Coupe and incorporate it into the Kindig CF1 Fastback as a concept-styled build. What if Cadillac used a 1953 Corvette as a platform for a Caddy sports car? It’s all built in and around one of Kindig’s carbon-fiber CF1 fastback bodies. We’re told it was surprisingly easy to make the longer, LS-based V-12 fit in the CF1’s engine bay. This time around, the CF1 is getting some special body mods. For the back of the “Caddyvette,” custom 1953 Cadillac-style taillight fins and taillights were added. The rear shadow box for the license plate was also moved and placed below the rear trim. The front grille takes inspiration from the 1953 Cadillac by adding Dagmars to bumperettes and “teeth” to the center grille. Once the body was just right, the new Caddy-inspired CF1 was shot in a new color called Oh Baby! Blue, which is a light pearlescent blue that will be coming out soon in Kindig’s Modern Classikk paint line powered by Sikkens. With weeks until SEMA, work continued on the Caddy CF1. Like all CF1s, this one rides on a full Roadster Shop CF1 Spec 7 chassis and is stopped by Wilwood binders. The massive 9.2L LS V-12 came from Race Cast in Australia and is topped with a 12-stack injection by Harrop. Backing up the V-12 is an 8HP70 ZF Bowler Transmission controlled by Turbo Lamik, while Haltech makes the engine side function. Kindig loves designing wheels, and this CF1 is no exception. The one-off wheels were designed by Dave Kindig, then brought to life by EVOD Industries. They pencil out at 21x9 inches for front and 22x12 inches for rear. The tires are Michelin Pilot Sport 4S in 255/30 and 335/25. For exhaust, the CF1 is running Borla mufflers with built-in X-pipe mated to a 3-inch stainless exhaust, also from Borla, made specifically for the CF1. Custom headers had to be fabricated to accommodate the V-12 powerplant. The interior was crafted by Seams Impossible Interiors in a cream-colored leather with a Sparc Industries steering wheel designed by Kindig to have a Caddy vibe. Before heading to SEMA, the CF1 will get side trim stylized after the 1953 Cadillac, as well as custom emblems. Look for this reimagined CF1 in the Kindig display, and we’ll be sure to snap a few pictures of the finished car when we check it out at the 2026 SEMA show. title: Deontay Wilder to face unbeaten Opetaia on Fury v Joshua undercard in Cardiff - The Guardian
content: Wilder, 41, has won 43 of his 45 victories by knockout Australian cruiserweight champion moves up in weight Deontay Wilder, the former World Boxing Council heavyweight champion, will face unbeaten Australian cruiserweight world champion Jai Opetaia on the undercard of Tyson Fury’s showdown with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December, organizers announced on Wednesday. Opetaia will move up to heavyweight to take on one of history’s most devastating punchers at the Principality Stadium with the event streaming live worldwide on Netflix. Wilder, 41, held the WBC’s version of the heavyweight title from 2015 to 2020, making 10 successful defenses before losing his belt to Fury. The American has a professional ledger of 45 wins, four defeats and one draw, with 43 victories coming by knockout. The 2008 Olympic bronze medalist from Tuscaloosa, Alabama, appeared bound for retirement after a one-sided defeat to Joseph Parker followed by a brutal knockout loss to Zhilei Zhang in 2024, but has since breathed extended life into his career with wins over journeyman Tyrrell Anthony Herndon and two-time world title challenger Derek Chisora. Opetaia, 31, is unbeaten in 31 professional outings and has established himself as the sport’s leading cruiserweight. The Australian southpaw captured the IBF world title with a victory over Mairis Briedis in 2022 and has since dominated all comers in the 200lb division. A former Olympian who represented Australia at the 2012 London Games aged 16, the Sydneysider will be making his heavyweight debut against Wilder, who stands 6ft 7in and has spent his entire professional career in the division. The matchup adds another high-profile contest to a card headlined by Fury and Joshua, whose long-awaited meeting was confirmed in September after years of unsuccessful negotiations. “The co-main event is officially set,” Zuffa Boxing’s Dana White, whose disputed role in the promotion remains uncertain, said on social media. “These two guys have a combined 67 knockouts. You do not want to miss this fight.” The undercard for Fury v Wilder will take place on a Friday night, with the main-event ringwalks at the Principality Stadium expected in the small hours of Saturday morning – widely reported to be around 2am. That is to accommodate a prime-time American audience for Netflix, which will broadcast it globally after its preferred plan to stage the fight at New York’s Madison Square Garden was scuppered. Both men are attempting to return to the summit of boxing’s prestige division after suffering two defeats apiece against Oleksandr Usyk, the unbeaten former undisputed heavyweight champion from Ukraine who relinquished his remaining world title belts in June but insists he has not retired. Fury has won twice since returning to the ring, while Joshua has spent the year rebuilding after his knockout loss to Daniel Dubois in 2024. The rivals came closest to meeting for the undisputed championship in 2021, but the fight collapsed after a US arbitrator ruled Fury was contractually obligated to face Wilder for a third time. Joshua subsequently lost his titles to Usyk, with several attempts to revive the Fury contest falling apart in the years since.

title: Real Salt Lake Hosts Must-Win Decision Day Game v LA Galaxy Saturday - Real Salt Lake
content: RSL Needs Three Points Plus Other Results to Continue Western Conference Postseason Streak; Claret-and-Cobalt Looking to Improve Upon 12W-4L-4T Record in Sandy on Nov. 7 “Decision Day”; Tickets for All Home Events Remain Available via www.RSL.com/Tickets HERRIMAN, Utah (Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026) – Saturday, Real Salt Lake (12W-15L-6T, 42 points, 11th West / 20th Shield MLS) returns home to host long-time rival LA Galaxy (11W-11L-11T, 44 points, 7th West / 15th Shield) for Major League Soccer’s 2026 “Decision Day,” as multiple games with postseason implications kick off simultaneously. RSL returns home for the MUST-WIN affair looking to improve upon the Claret-and-Cobalt’s 12-4-4 (W-L-T) record this year on Utah soil, looking to vanquish the Galaxy for the fifth time at home in seven meetings during the Pablo Mastroeni era. RSL looks to rebound from its 2-1 loss in San Jose Saturday, a match which snapped a four-game unbeaten run and a 4-1-1 mark that saw it secure 13 points from those last six games to vault itself back into the Western Conference postseason race. RSL now sits just one point shy of Portland Timbers, Seattle Sounders and Colorado Rapids for the final playoff spots in the West, needing a win Saturday and for at least one of the three to drop points. RSL can still finish as high as seventh in the West, with a win against the Galaxy and dropped points from all of Portland, Seattle and Colorado. If even one of them drop points, RSL will extend the Club’s postseason qualification streak to a West-best six seasons, eight of the last nine year overall, and 16 of 19 campaigns dating back to its inaugural playoff foray in 2008. Saturday’s RSL v LA Galaxy contest on Apple TV features Christian Miles and Kacey White on the primary English-language call, while Jorge Perez-Navarro and Marcelo Balboa will provide the Spanish-language analysis. Simultaneously, the KSL Radio team of David James and Jay Nolly return to the mic, with Manuel Hernández conducting the Spanish call with Willy Barrueta and Isidro López on KBMG Latino 106.3 FM. GAME NOTES for Saturday’s RSL v LA Galaxy Match Available Online The Adobe PDF version of the 2026 RSL Game Guide in advance of Saturday’s contest between Real Salt Lake and LA Galaxy can be found HERE. Media members looking to receive the document as an attachment or have further questions are asked to please contact RSL Communications via email at RSLcommunications@RSL.com. Saturday, RSL welcomes the return of Designated Player Morgan Guilavogui, who missed the San Jose match due to his yellow-card accumulation suspension, with the Guinean international providing three goals and adding three assists during the recent six-game RSL surge. Now with 18 goals across all competitions and 14 in his debut MLS campaign, RSL rookie and 2026 Golden Boot leader Sergi Solans needs just one goal Saturday to match the 2012 record for total goals, 19, set by Club legend Alvaro Saborio. Should Solan burst out with a hat trick Saturday, his three goals would match the all-time Club-best scoring campaigns (17 goals by Arango, 2024; Saborio, 2012), as well as the MLS all-time rookie record of 17 goals (Cyle Larin, Orlando, 2015). Saturday could also mark the first home start since May 16 for homegrown DF Justen Glad, who has appeared in each of the three games in his return from an adductor injury suffered on May 23 at Minnesota, coming off the bench in the recent wins against St. Louis and Austin, before starting and playing 60 minutes in San Jose. Fellow DF Lukas Engel also returned from his hamstring injury on Saturday, playing the final 30 minutes at Earthquakes, while winger Zach Booth suffered a dislocated shoulder, with his status questionable for Decision Day. Real Salt Lake Head Coach Pablo Mastroeni has now managed the Club in 220 matches across all competitions, registering 89 wins, 81 losses and 51 draws in MLS, Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, Leagues Cup, Open Cup, Concacaf Champions Cup and international friendly contests since late August, 2021. The former U.S. Men’s National Team World Cup standout (2002, 2006), MLS Cup Champion (2010) as a player, and former Colorado Rapids manager (2014-16) has averaged 1.60 points per game with RSL in his 221 matches at the helm. Only Cup-winning former manager Jason Kreis (2007-13) – now the Club’s President of Soccer – boasts more games, more wins and a higher PPG average than Mastroeni in RSL’s 22 seasons. During the Mastroeni era, resilience, grit and determination have served as trademarks for RSL, with the Club suffering back-to-back losses on just 25 occasions in those 221 games. The October 17 road win at Kansas City marked the latest opportunity for the Claret-and-Cobalt to display its “xDAWG” mentality to earn the result, now winning 37 and drawing 19 times in “bounce-back” games following a loss in Mastroeni’s five-plus seasons in Utah. Drawing first blood has also proven to be critical for RSL during the five-plus seasons under Mastroeni, with RSL now 59-12-23 (W-L-T) when scoring first. title: Colom v. Hyde-Smith: When—and how—will this close contest be decided? - the mississippi independent
content: Editor’s note: As of 5:44 pm on Nov. 4, the Associated Press reported that Scott Colom’s lead has grown. With 96 percent of the votes counted, he now has 464,926 votes, or 49 percent, while Cindy Hyde-Smith has 463,788, or 48.9 percent. AP updates can be monitored here. The astonishing closeness of the U.S. Senate election between Democrat Scott Colom and incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith is making national news even amid the intensive coverage of the electoral earthquake that will give Democrats control of the U.S. House and Senate. There are multiple reasons for the attention, but chief among them is that the election is so close, illustrating, perhaps as much as any race ever has, that every vote matters. Colom’s lead also provides an exclamation point to the larger Democratic juggernaut, given that he is a Black Democrat in a state with a charged racial history that has for decades voted decidedly Republican in statewide elections and which voted for President Donald Trump by more than 20 points in 2024. Among national outlets, the Wall Street Journal reported on Colom’s “wafer-thin lead” over Hyde-Smith by just 43 votes as of 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time, Nov. 4, with more than 945,000 (about 95 percent) of the ballots counted. The narrow margin means the vote might come down to provisional ballots, which could take days to review, the Journal noted. In Mississippi, counties must certify their votes by Nov. 13 and the Secretary of State’s office declares the final results on Dec. 3. Under Mississippi law, a recount can be ordered only by court order, the Journal reported. Mississippi, in fact, has never passed a recount law. No Democrat has won a Senate race in the state since John Stennis in 1982. Affidavit ballots in the current Senate race are still under review, and mail ballots postmarked by Election Day can arrive for five more business days—a window that the U.S. Supreme Court upheld in June in Watson v. Republican National Committee. If the final margin stays this close, the losing candidate will find that Mississippi offers fewer ways to potentially challenge the outcome than almost any other state. Mississippi has no recount law at all, automatic or requested. Election law scholar Derek Muller noted overnight that the state’s election code also contains no procedure for contesting a general election for Congress. For Mississippians, that means the question of who represents them in the U.S. Senate could be settled in Washington, D.C. by senators from other states. Mississippi’s election code lays out three kinds of contests: party primaries, county offices and legislative seats. A losing candidate in a party primary can contest the result under Section 23-15-923, first before the party’s executive committee and then in court. Chris McDaniel took that road after losing the 2014 Republican Senate runoff to Thad Cochran. A special circuit judge threw out the case, and the Mississippi Supreme Court affirmed that in October 2014, holding that a 1959 decision, Kellum v. Johnson, gave candidates 20 days to file (McDaniel waited more than twice that long). Section 23-15-951 lets a voter or candidate contest an election for an office within a county by petition in circuit court. Two routes are still open in the relevant U.S. Senate race. The first is litigation over specific ballots. A campaign can go to court under state or federal law over decisions to count or to reject particular affidavit or mailed ballots. A ruling there can change the vote totals. The second is in the U.S. Senate. Article I, Section 5 of the U.S. Constitution makes each chamber of Congress the judge of the elections, returns and qualifications of its members. In Roudebush v. Hartke in 1972, the U.S. Supreme Court allowed Indiana to run a recount in a disputed Senate race, holding that the Senate kept the power to make its own judgment after a state recount. Since then, most states have written recount and contest procedures for federal races. The Senate’s own record shows how long that kind of judgment can take. In New Hampshire in 1974, Republican Louis Wyman and Democrat John Durkin traded the lead through two recounts, and the state ballot commission finally put Wyman ahead by two votes. Durkin petitioned the Senate in December 1974. The Rules Committee deadlocked, the full Senate deadlocked, and after seven months the Senate declared the seat vacant. New Hampshire held a new election in September 1975 and Durkin won it by more than 27,000 votes. A vacancy in a Mississippi’s U.S. Senate seat would put the seat in the hands of the governor until a new election. Gov. Phil Bryant used that appointment power in 2018 to send Hyde-Smith to the Senate after Cochran resigned. The state has watched a legislative body decide its elections twice in living memory. On Jan. 4, 1965, the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party challenged the seating of the state’s five white congressmen. Fannie Lou Hamer, Annie Devine and Victoria Gray argued that the men had been elected in districts where Black Mississippians were kept from voting. The House Elections Subcommittee took depositions across the state for months. On Sept. 17, 1965, the full House voted 228 to 143 to dismiss the challenge and keep the delegation in its seats. The second case ran through the Mississippi Senate, and Hyde-Smith was part of it. In December 2003, Richard White contested the certified election of Dwayne Thomas in Hinds County’s Senate District 29. The Senate created a special committee of five senators, including Hyde-Smith, who was then a state senator from Brookhaven, to hear the case. After three days of hearings in January 2004, the committee found that errors in the November election made it impossible to determine what District 29’s voters had chosen. The full Senate refused to seat Thomas and ordered Hinds County to hold a new election between the two men on Feb. 10, 2004. That same session, a state House bill to let party executive committees recount ballots in primary contests died in committee. Recount bills have died the same way since. In January, Rep. Timmy Ladner, a Republican, filed House Bill 1026, which would have required a recount, by a different method from the original count, in any race decided by 250 votes or 1 percent of the total, whichever was greater. It died in the House Apportionment and Elections Committee on Feb. 3. Under that bill, a 43-vote margin in a race with nearly a million ballots would have triggered a recount automatically. County election commissions will spend the coming days reviewing affidavit ballots, and each county will then certify its results to the Secretary of State. Any lawsuit over individual ballots would come during that canvass. If the margin holds in the dozens, the question would go to the Senate that convenes on Jan. 3, 2027. Mississippi’s lawmakers have had opportunities to write their own answer since at least 2004, during the same session that their own Senate threw out a certified result in Hinds County, and they have let each bill die in committee. Perhaps no one in power expected to need one. Republicans have won every U.S. Senate race in the state since Trent Lott took an open seat in 1988, most of them by double digits. If this count holds, the U.S. Senate will decide who holds the seat. But a lot could change in the meantime, as a result of the counting of affidavit and mail-in ballots. A version of this article appeared in Derrion Arrington’s Substack “America is Mississippi.” NBC has said that Hyde-Smith would need to win 49% of the remaining vote in order to catch up to Colom; how can someone catch up by getting less than half of the remaining votes?? A new casting rumor suggests that two Peacemaker fan-favorites will return for the upcoming HBO Max series. Scooper @ApocHorseman shared the report on X (Twitter) and wrote, "EXCLUSIVE: Vigilante And Judomaster Are Set To Return In The People V. Gorilla Grodd." EXCLUSIVE: Vigilante And Judomaster Are Set To Return In 'The People V. Gorilla Grodd' pic.twitter.com/yswop0MkzS — Apocalyptic Horseman (@ApocHorseman) November 4, 2026 According to the report, Freddie Stroma and Nhut Le each filmed their respective scenes in a single day, indicating their appearances in the eight-part series will likely be brief cameos. DC Studios has not officially confirmed the report. Stroma plays Adrian Chase, better known as Vigilante, while Le portrays Judomaster. Both characters appeared alongside John Cena's Christopher Smith in Peacemaker. Their reported return would bring two familiar supporting characters into the new DCU story. Vigilante is a highly skilled fighter who takes the law into his own hands as a self-appointed crime fighter. His personality and unwavering loyalty to Peacemaker also make him a source of comic relief. Meanwhile, Judomaster is a trained martial artist who initially finds himself at odds with Peacemaker and his team. The characters also have long histories in DC Comics. Writer Marv Wolfman and artist George Pérez created Adrian Chase, who first appeared in The New Teen Titans #23 in 1982. He later debuted as Vigilante in The New Teen Titans Annual #2 in 1983. Judomaster first appeared in Charlton Comics' Special War Series #4 in 1965. Writer Joe Gill and artist Frank McLaughlin created the character, whose original identity was Rip Jagger. His comic book debut came more than a decade before Adrian Chase's first appearance. Meanwhile, The People v. Gorilla Grodd will center on Jimmy Olsen, played by Skyler Gisondo. title: 5 key matchups to watch in Jaguars v. Ravens in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports

title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia added to undercard in Cardiff - BBC
content: Deontay Wilder is almost 10 years older than Jai Opetaia American Deontay Wilder will fight Australia's Jai Opetaia on the undercard of Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua in December. The bout will serve as the co-main event for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight, with the WBA 'super' heavyweight title on the line at Cardiff's Principality Stadium. Unbeaten WBA 'regular' cruiserweight champion Opetaia, 31, will step up to heavyweight for the first time to fight Wilder, a former world champion with 43 knockouts. Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) will hope to re-establish himself among the heavyweight elite, while Opetaia (31-0, 24 KOs) could be eyeing a fresh challenge, after years of dominance at cruiserweight. Wilder, 41, held the WBC heavyweight title from 2015 to 2020 and is regarded as one of the most feared punchers of his generation. The American also enjoyed an epic trilogy with Fury, but came out on the losing side with a draw and two defeats. Wilder had also been close to facing Joshua but a knockout loss against China's Zhilei Zhang in June 2024 derailed the potential bout. Tickets for the main event sold out in under an hour, despite the ringwalks being expected to start around 01:00 GMT on Saturday, 12 December, following a short live music performance, and the stadium will remain open until 03:30. The remaining bouts on the undercard are still to be announced, with Wales' former IBF super-featherweight champion Joe Cordina thought to be in negotiations to fight Manny Pacquiao. This will be a first high-level heavyweight fight for Opetaia, who is a previous holder of the IBF championship and a force at cruiserweight. A move to Zuffa Boxing has brought complications for the Australian - who stopped WBC champion Noel Mikaelian in September but could not claim his belt due to a sanctioning dispute. Opetaia faced off against David Benavidez after his victory over Mikaelian and a future cruiserweight fight could still happen if the Mexican comes through his three-belt unification bout with Michal Cieslak. For Wilder, this presents a chance to be the first professional boxer to get the better of Opetaia. Wilder has lost two of his previous four fights, but picked up a win last time out with a split-decision win over Briton Derek Chisora in April. title: Viral Kid Podcasters Hen-Dawg and Jimmy V React to a Surprise from TODAY Anchors, and You Have to See Their Faces - TODAY.com

Up to 63% Off Summer Fridays, Glossier, More Viral Kid Podcasters Hen-Dawg and Jimmy V React to a Surprise from TODAY Anchors, and You Have to See Their Faces They’ve interviewed an NFL Hall of Famer and gotten an autograph from Chicago Bears star Caleb Williams, but kid podcasters Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg were left speechless by a surprise on TODAY. Henry “Hen-Dawg” Zotti and Jimmy “V” Maley, both 10, are diehard Chicago Bears fans, the middle school heirs to the iconic Bill Swerski’s Superfans on “Saturday Night Live” in their love for Da Bears. Despite their devotion to the black and orange, Hen-Dawg had never even been to a Bears game — until now. The boys were surprised by Craig Melvin, Savannah Guthrie and Carson Daly during a video call on TODAY Nov. 4 when they were gifted tickets to the Bears’ Sunday Night Football game on Nov. 8 against the visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Hen-Dawg’s face went blank in disbelief as the surprise started to sink in. Jimmy V’s mother then entered the room with two tickets for the boys, who yelled in delight before sharing a delirious hug. “We’re going to kill ‘em this weekend!” Hen-Dawg said. The boys will surely have some fresh content for their podcast after their trip to Chicago’s legendary Soldier Field. They already have interviewed Hall of Famer former Bears linebacker Brian Urlacher and received a signed copy of the Madden 27 video game from current Bears star quarterback Caleb Williams. Hen-Dawg also dressed as Williams for Halloween this year. The tandem made their TODAY debut in September, becoming instant fan favorites with their straight talk. They also have become mini celebrities at school. “The older kids that have phones usually ask for pictures,” Jimmy V said. It’s not easy to knock them off their game like Savannah, Craig and Carson did with their surprise, considering they don’t get starstruck. Urlacher is one of the greatest linebackers in NFL history and a Bears icon, but they talked to him like anybody else. “Just another podcast with another person,” Jimmy V said. “Just talking to a first-ballot Hall of Famer, nothing much.” They also have plenty to discuss this year, as the Bears are off to a 6-2 start. They recently traded for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and just walloped the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday Night Football. The way the Bears have been playing has the boys thinking this is the year they will finally win their first Super Bowl since their legendary 1985 team. They believe Chicago will do it in honor of franchise legend Mike Ditka, a Hall of Fame Bears player and coach who died at 86 on Oct. 9. “Mike Ditka from the stars is going to to watch us win it all,” Jimmy V said. title: This V-16 Resurrects a Forgotten Engine Architecture for a Custom Build - Car and Driver
content: Most things in life come down to timing, including dialing in the firing order of a V-16 made from two LS3 V-8s. “If you have two V-8s that are exactly in the same timing, your pistons aren’t firing properly; it can rip itself apart—not good.” That’s Bryan Fuller summarizing the challenges presented by physically joining a pair of LS3 V-8 engines to create an 854 cubic-inch V-16 reported to make in the neighborhood of 1200 horsepower. But while getting 16 holes to fire in a complementary, non-destructive manner is a feat unto itself, the impetus behind the project is a one-off custom Roadster designed by Hot Wheels with direct input from the unnamed, ostensibly well-heeled client. Fuller says the design of the 19.5-foot-long custom roadster is inspired by the 1938 Cadillac V-16 Series-90, but devotees of the brand’s history will recognize the spirit of the 1937 Cadillac V16 Hartmann Cabriolet, a two-off run of vehicles crafted in Switzerland for—you guessed it—a wealthy client. Back in the 21st century, Fuller had to address the timing, cooling, fuel, and air issues, as well as engineer their structural unity and their combined output to ensure the V-8s play nicely together. As for ignition timing, the rear engine is clocked back “about 45 degrees,” which allows the tandem V-8s to fire in the proper order of a V-16. A single starter spins both. The mating of the torque is achieved by mounting a giubo joint (a.k.a. flex disc), a flex joint comprised of a rubber or urethane center with metal mounting plates on either side that mates the rear of the front engine with the front of the rear engine. Structural connection of the V-8s is made via a trio of CNC-machined plates, one in the center valley and one each on the lower right and left sides. Ignition is handled traditionally, with two computers and individual plug wires, Fuller noted that “the LS3 is a known quantity,” and years of tuning the LS3 V-8 makes the job a little easier. Cooling is the only shared major system. A Meziere water pump generates enough pressure to move the coolant through both engines, out a custom dual outlet, and into a single radiator. Air is handled by a highly modified Holley intake that will continue to be modified as the project moves to installing the powertrain in the body. The Tremec T-56 Magnum transmission was optimized by Bowler Performance Transmissions, who polished the internals, among other tweaks. As expected, ARP hardware is utilized throughout the project. Even the powertrain table it sits on is custom-built. At this point, the V-16 is waiting for the Roadster Shop to finish the custom chassis so the team can begin the process of combining all three elements to create a fully operational vehicle. How long that process will take is unclear, but the V-16 makes a pretty nice conversation piece just as it sits on its custom display stand. title: This Slammed ’55 Chevy Bel Air Restomod Packs a 598-Cubic-Inch V-8 with 741 HP - Car and Driver
content: Built by CAL Automotive Creations and featuring a giant V-8, this ‘55 Chevy was among the many custom builds shown at SEMA. People have been modifying classic cars for ages, and the Chevy Bel Air is a perfect candidate. CAL Automotive Creations got its hands on a 1955 two-door model and decided it needed a massive V-8, which BluePrint Engines was happy to provide. Paired with a Bowler automatic gearbox, the crate engine is covered in deep red paint and outfitted with an EFI intake, machined valve covers, and fabricated stainless-steel headers. The 598-cubic-inch V-8, which produces 741 horsepower and 703 pound-feet of torque, breathes through SpinTech mufflers. Additionally, CAL thoroughly reworked the Art Morrison chassis, creating rear rails that turn upward for a lower ride height in combination with RideTech coil-overs. Raising the center crossmembers ensure that components remain above the scrub line, meaning it’s drivable even on pockmarked roads. Of course, the exterior received attention as well. Reshaped quarter panels, taillight bezels, and a front grille surround are examples of where CAL demonstrated its craftsmanship. The dark paint and bodywork were specially made for this build, accompanied by nickel touches from Advanced Plating. Leading Edge Machine and Design is responsible for the one-off wheels, which match the paint. A staggered setup gives the Bel Air an even more aggressive look. The interior was a product of CAL and Santana Interior Design, and though the cabin still has a classic look with its billet-machined center console (featuring cupholders under the slidable armrest), it is equipped with Dakota digital instrumentation and Vintage Air climate control. As far as restomods go, this one has almost no stones left unturned. With a degree in multimedia journalism and a passion for the automotive world, Mason Cordell enjoys driving, wrenching, writing, and everything in between. He keeps a running note sheet titled "cars for collection" and already owns a ‘95 Miata and an ‘08 M5. Clearly, he has a problem. title: Ireland v Argentina: Craig Casey, Nick Timoney and Sean Jansen all to start against Pumas - BBC
content: Ireland resume their Nations Championship campaign against Argentina in Dublin on Friday night Nick Timoney, Craig Casey and Sean Jansen will start for Ireland against Argentina in the Nations Championship on Friday night, with Jamison Gibson-Park and Josh van der Flier on the bench at Aviva Stadium. With captain Caelan Doris and two-tour British and Irish Lion Jack Conan missing through injury, Connacht's Jansen always seemed the most likely to fill in at number eight for head coach Andy Farrell. The 27-year-old made a try-scoring debut for Ireland against Japan in July and followed that with a cameo as a replacement against the All Blacks a week later. The selections of Casey and Timoney, however, were less expected. Influential scrum-half Gibson-Park has arguably been Ireland's best performer in recent seasons. The 34-year-old missed the start of Leinster's season with a groin injury but made his return in the win over Munster on 24 October. With only that game under his belt this season, he will start on the bench with Casey preferred to start at nine in a half-back partnership with fly-half Sam Prendergast, who has recovered from a wrist injury. Ulster back row Timoney, 31, previously struggled to regularly break into the side despite strong form for his province, but selection against Argentina means he will be involved in his ninth consecutive Test. Seven of those appearances, however, have been from the bench and his start on Friday night comes at the expense of former World Rugby player of the year Van der Flier. Farrell on selection calls and 'exciting' World Cup journey Live commentary on BBC Radio Ulster, BBC Sport website and app With Garry Ringrose ruled out because of a hamstring problem, the experienced Robbie Henshaw will wear the 13 jersey, forming a midfield partnership with Stuart McCloskey. Wing Mack Hansen, prop Andrew Porter and Ryan Baird all start, having not featured for Ireland since the defeat by South Africa in November 2025. All three missed the Six Nations and summer fixtures in the Nations Championship through injury. Hansen starts in the number 11 jersey in what is Ireland's first home game since James Lowe's departure from Irish rugby, with Robert Baloucoune keeping his spot on the right wing and Hugo Keenan selected at full-back. Baird is selected at blind-side flanker, joining Timoney and Jansen in the back row. Porter's return at loose-head will be a considerable boost for coach Farrell after recent windows were impact by injury problems at the position. He will pack down alongside hooker Dan Sheehan, who captains the side in Doris' absence, and tight-head Tadhg Furlong. Furlong is free to play after he was cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin last month. With Tadhg Beirne and Joe McCarthy selected as starting locks, James Ryan must make do with a place on the bench alongside Van der Flier and Gibson-Park. Sam Illo, who will make his home debut if called upon, Ronan Kelleher, Tom O'Toole, Ciaran Frawley and Bundee Aki are Ireland's other replacements. Argentina boss Felipe Contepomi has made 12 changes from the side that drew 28-28 with Australia in September as Los Pumas seek a first away win over Ireland. Toulouse full-back Juan Cruz Mallia returns to win a first cap since November 2025 after injury. Ireland: Hugo Keenan; Robert Baloucoune, Robbie Henshaw, Stuart McCloskey, Mack Hansen; Sam Prendergast, Craig Casey; Andrew Porter, Dan Sheehan (capt), Tadhg Furlong; Joe McCarthy, Tadhg Beirne; Ryan Baird, Nick Timoney, Sean Jansen. Replacements: Ronan Kelleher, Tom O'Toole, Sam Illo, James Ryan, Josh van der Flier, Jamison Gibson-Park, Ciaran Frawley or Jamie Benson, Bundee Aki. Argentina: Juan Cruz Mallia; Bautista Delguy, Justo Piccardo, Santiago Chocobares, Mateo Carreras; Tomas Albornoz, Gonzalo Garcia; Boris Wenger, Julian Montoya (capt), Francisco Moreno; Guido Petti, Pedro Rubiolo; Juan Martin Gonzalez, Marcos Kremer, Pablo Matera. title: The V-8 Hall of Shame: 7 Engines That Let Drivers Down - MotorTrend
content: These eight-cylinder stinkers underperformed their way into oblivion. Not all V-8 engines are created equal. Scouring the annals of automotive history reveals more than a few eight-cylinder options that drew the scorn and anger of owners who were bamboozled by advanced technologies that couldn’t deliver, poor design choices that crippled performance, or bad construction that led to serious repairs—or sometimes all three. Here’s our look at the seven V-8 engines that have the worst reputations in automotive history, with an explanation of exactly how and why these duds made it to the market in the first place, and when they eventually shuffled off into obscurity. The automotive industry is littered with casualties from the early adoption of primitive electronic engine controls that engineering teams didn’t truly grasp how to execute in the real world. In the mid-1970s, Chrysler served up a prime example of trying to do too much, too soon, with a technology called Lean-Burn, which it installed on the 400-cubic-inch V-8 engines that served as the backbone of its sedan lineup (and eventually pushed onto every other V-8 in the fleet, too). The idea was simple: advance or slow engine timing on an engine that ran lean (i.e., with as little fuel in the air/fuel mixture as possible) to avoid having to install expensive emissions equipment. To do this, it used eight sensors that kept track of throttle position and its rate of change, engine temperature, the temperature of the air entering the intake, and the motor’s starting condition. It then fed that data to a computer that tried to vary ignition timing to achieve cleaner tailpipe emissions. Did any of the above work? Absolutely not. For starters, Chrysler chose to attach the Lean-Burn analog computer to the engine’s air cleaner, which shook it like a hunting dog and heated it up like the surface of the sun. This rendered its carefully considered calculations so much gobbledygook, to the point where its very lean carburetor design could no longer balance power and emissions. Sick of limping home, most owners banished Lean-Burn tech by their own hands (or those of their mechanic). Chrysler moved to more sophisticated, and reliable, versions of the Lean-Burn concept in the early 1980s, but the previous decade’s implementation dealt it a black eye that turned many buyers off the automaker’s offerings. While turbodiesel engines are no longer uncommon, in the 1970s they had yet to penetrate the American mindset outside of the heavy truck and commercial equipment crowd. Sensing the opportunity to solve its fuel efficiency woes (no easy task for a company that had long relied on large-displacement V-8s in nearly every segment), General Motors turned to diesel technology in its passenger vehicles. Unfortunately, in a reflection of GM’s business approach in that era, it decided to cut as many corners as possible when bringing these new diesel engines to market. Did we say new? Sorry, we meant “converting Oldsmobile’s 350-cubic-inch gas V-8 to run on diesel fuel,” a process that ignored the need to strengthen the motor to deal with the intense compression required to initiate diesel combustion, or to add a water separator to deal with lower-quality diesel fuel. Largely untested and certainly poorly thought-out, these engines arrived for the 1978 model year and quickly began blowing their head gaskets and destroying their fuel systems from the inside out due to moisture accumulation. Even when perfectly functional—perhaps in the first five minutes after purchase—these 120-horsepower laggards smoked and stumbled their way down the road to the delight of absolutely no one, whether behind the wheel or stuck in traffic staring at the tailpipe. Unfortunately for GM, Oldsmobile’s diesel V-8 option was initially popular with unsuspecting customers and was offered in nearly 30 different vehicles across nearly every one of its sister brands. The ubiquity of its failure turned American drivers off diesel passenger cars for decades. Remember what we said about reach exceeding grasp when it comes to complex engine controls? Our next two entries tread similar ground to Chrysler’s Lean-Burn strategy, while differing in the size of their respective ambitions. Having tried to outrun smog equipment with big-block cubic inches in its Firebird Trans Am muscle cars for most of the 1970s, for 1980 Pontiac looked to forced induction as a potential way forward. A turbocharger was outfitted to a 301-cubic-inch V-8 engine whose compression was lowered to help deal with the boost. It was also given stronger internals and a more capacious oil pump to push it onto the performance stage from the meek and mild position it had previously held in the lineup. The trouble with the turbo V-8? Its carburetor simply couldn’t reliably enrich the fuel supply when the engine was in boost, even though its four-barrel Rochester was designed to monitor the amount of air being forced into the engine. This meant that when push came to shove, Pontiac drivers frequently encountered detonation, otherwise known as knock, a dangerous condition for the engine that forced the Trans Am’s electronic spark controller to severely dial back ignition timing to prevent permanent damage. The end result was a performance car that couldn’t really perform, at least not reliably, a sad fact that was reflected in the inconsistent test results from automotive media in its era and complaints from owners dealing with low-octane fuel and a shaky engine that seemed scared of boost. Pontiac pulled the model after its second year following disappointing sales. The reigning champion of cautionary V-8 technology tales is, of course, Cadillac’s V8-6-4 “displacement on demand” engine. Dubbed the L62, it was deployed across the automaker’s entire 1981 lineup and was touted as the last word in delivering both power and efficiency in the same package. The thinking was simple: design an engine that could turn its cylinders off, in pairs, when they weren’t needed, thus cutting down on the amount of fuel being consumed during simple cruising. If this sounds familiar, it’s because General Motors revisited the concept in the 2000s with greater success. At the time, however, computer controls simply couldn’t handle the complex range of variables that presented themselves during basic driving and thus could not be relied on to properly drop and pick up cylinders as needed. Despite boasting hundreds of thousands of calculations per second from the hardware managing the L62 V-8, the promised 30 percent boost in fuel economy was a myth. The reality was an engine that bucked, hesitated, and otherwise made smooth driving almost completely impossible. Even at steady highway speeds, the system would snap back and forth between four- and eight-cylinder operations, alternatively soaking the cylinders with fuel and starving them. Try as they might, Cadillac’s engineers couldn’t find a way to make the V8-6-4 system work, and after an extensive attempt at reprogramming after the engine went on sale, it was banished by the end of the model year. General Motors then gave existing owners the opportunity to have the variable-displacement system permanently disabled. Perhaps the company should have tested it under real-world conditions at some point? Not every bad V-8 design in the early 1980s was done in by poor electronics. Ford enjoyed a decent run of small-block eight-cylinder engines in its Mustang coupe and convertible starting in the mid-1960s, and while this family of motors might have gone through some tepid times the following decade due to nascent emissions equipment, their fundamentals remained solid. In 1980, Ford was in the second model year of the Fox-generation Mustang, which eventually helped revitalize the automaker’s moribund performance reputation. Sadly, before that could happen, the car was saddled with a 4.2-liter version of the company’s venerable small-block that stood in stark contrast to the lauded “5.0” V-8 that was to follow. Also known as the 255 (its displacement in cubic inches), the 4.2-liter motor looks a lot like other Ford small-blocks. Tear one down, though, and you’ll discover low-compression combustion chambers born from a time when low-quality fuel ruled the day, matched with choked intake ports edging it toward frugality rather than performance. Everything about this engine was intended to boost mpg and drop emissions at the expense of horsepower. With roughly 120 horsepower on tap, it was the lowest-output factory V-8 to ever grace a Mustang engine bay. A few other Fox-platform cars were also cursed with the 4.2-liter engine, and stories abounded of owners unable to maintain a steady speed uphill with the pedal floored when tooling around in their Fairmonts and LTDs. As Ford muddled through rebranding its compact as a reborn muscle car, it was clear the Mustang’s 302-cubic-inch engine was due for a return. In less than two years, the 302 was back on the order sheet alongside the 255, and soon after that the HO version of the 5.0 V-8 made the 4.2-liter a distant memory. General Motors also flirted with its own underpowered V-8 around the same time as Mustang owners were suffering. This unit, which notably produced just 10 horsepower more than the base V-6 in the 1980–'81 Pontiac Firebird, was derived from the previously mentioned 301-cubic-inch V-8, albeit without a turbo attached. Like the Ford 4.2, Pontiac’s LS5 V-8 was the product of the previous decade’s energy crisis. It shrunk the bores of the 301 and followed a similar playbook in terms of tamping down on airflow and compression. It produced the same amount of power as the anemic Mustang—120 horses—but there was little to no fuel efficiency benefit, with the engine delivering almost identical consumption compared to the larger 307-cubic-inch Oldsmobile V-8 that outgunned it in that sister brand’s showroom. The saddest aspect of the LS5 is that it and the 301 were the last two in-house V-8 engines ever developed by Pontiac. Following their two-year run, GM forced Pontiac to embrace eight-cylinder engines built by Chevrolet and Oldsmobile, and by the end of the automaker’s run in the late 2000s, it had fully ceded drivetrain development to the corporate mothership. The LS5 was a terrible way to end a glorious performance history. In the 1990s, BMW offered a V-8 engine in two different displacements in its North American catalog. The M60 was available in either a 3.0-liter or 4.0-liter edition, and it could be had in the likes of the 5 and 7 Series sedans, as well as the 8 Series coupe. The engine itself was a solid design, but its construction hid a fatal flaw. BMW chose to line the M60’s cylinders with something called Nikasil, or nickel silicon carbide. When exposed to high sulfur fuel—which was much more common in North America than it was in Europe—Nikasil begins to corrode and break down, eliminating any protection between the aluminum cylinder walls and the engine’s chromed-steel piston rings. What did this mean for BMW owners? Rough idle, loss of compression, and rapid oil consumption all indicated fatal wear of the cylinder walls, eventually leading to a loss of power and even bricked motors that couldn’t muster up enough compression to turn over. Nikasil caused so many problems for customers that the automaker was forced to recall and replace these linings with Alusil, an aluminum silicon alloy instead, adding another six years of warranty protection to affected powertrains. Today, it’s a bit of a wild west situation when trying to determine whether the used BMW you’re looking at has had the proper Alusil replacement linings installed. It’s an issue that also bled over into the M62 era, which was the V-8 powerplant for the E39-generation 5 Series, but only a very small number of those engines feature Nikasil, versus the entire production run of the M60. title: Fenerbahce v Liverpool: Team news - Liverpool FC
content:
Being ‘good in our press’ will be fundamental to Andoni Iraola’s team selection for Liverpool’s clash with Fenerbahce. The Reds face the Turkish side away from home on Wednesday evening, aiming to make it four wins in a row in the Champions League’s league phase. A 22-man travelling squad departed John Lennon Airport for Istanbul on Tuesday morning. Ryan Gravenberch was not included due to a heel injury for which he is receiving treatment at the AXA Training Centre. Head coach Iraola explained: “It’s a fracture of the heel. It’s about the pain. He has been with some discomfort. The other day against Arsenal he was warming up and he was not fully confident. “He hasn’t improved since then. But it’s going to be something that every day we ask him, every day we see how he is.” The boss was asked at his pre-match press conference if Trey Nyoni therefore could continue to feature in midfield in the enforced absence of Gravenberch. “He is playing most of the games – or even all the games lately – so we trust him,” came the reply. “He is doing very well and I think we have to encourage him to continue – to continue improving, continue learning, continue adding experience. He is in a very good place.” Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo are unavailable having not been named in the Reds’ submitted ‘A’ squad for the league phase. A muscle issue is currently sidelining Jeremie Frimpong, while Conor Bradley, Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni continue to recover from long-term injuries. On the challenge he expects from the hosts, Iraola added: “Fenerbahce is a team that has very good players. In the midfield they have a very good technical level. “If we allow them a lot of time on the ball or we don’t press them properly, we are going to suffer. I think we have to be good in our press, I think we have to try to control the game, don’t allow them to win confidence, because also they are experienced players, they know how to play these kind of games in this competition. “The stronger we start, the less chances we should give to Fenerbahce, because otherwise they are going to be dangerous.” Fenerbahce are under the guidance of interim head coach Dirk Kuyt at present. The former Liverpool forward – who returned to the Turkish side as an assistant in the summer, having previously had a three-year spell with them as a player – was appointed to the role last week. He will be without the experience of defender Nathan Ake and midfielder Marco Asensio against the Reds, with the pair injured. Jayden Oosterwolde has been out of action since August and there is a doubt over the availability of Kojo Peprah Oppong. Fenerbahce are seeking their first win of the league phase and come into this game on the back of consecutive 2-1 defeats in Turkiye’s top flight. Kuyt said at his pre-match press conference: “Romelu [Lukaku] was speaking about how important it is to show the fans – who deserve much more – a reaction of positive energy and a good performance. “We have really good players but we need to show up. When we show up tomorrow with good energy, with passion and there to play, I think it can be a very special night.” Fenerbahce 1-2 Goztepe (October 31): Ederson, Semedo, Skriniar, Oppong, Mercan, Kante, Guendouzi, Aydin, Kahveci, Akturkoglu, Lukaku. Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal (November 1): Alisson, Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Nyoni, Mac Allister, Wirtz, Gakpo, Barcola, Isak.
